messages:
elaine: Quick check-in on the postmortem action items for the KV residency + OOM runs from last week. Postmortem here: https://confluence.internal/r/kvr-postmortem. Owners listed in the doc: Sam (profiling), Munir (eviction limits), Ciaran (GC/frag), Kevin (canary). Status updates please.

sam: Did an initial flame/heap sampling on the repro cluster this morning. Found repeated hot allocations coming from the async batcher when prefix-caching misses. Sample snapshot:

```
# pmap-sample (top alloc sites)
0x7f9d2a..  42%  runtime.mallocgc
0x7f9d3b..  18%  github.com/redwood/serving/batcher.(*Batch).append
0x7f9d4c..  12%  github.com/redwood/cache/prefix.(*Shard).allocItem
```

sam: Hypothesis: the batcher is creating short-lived objects that end up in the same slab class, causing fragmentation under sustained load. Next step: add sampling to the canary and collect continuous heap samples for 6 hours. ETA: EOD Tue.

munir: Rolled eviction tuning PR to staging (https://git.internal/patches/CR-4221). Changes: shard_soft_limit bumped from 0.6 -> 0.72, shard_hard_limit unchanged, eviction_policy now LRU-protected for recent prefixes. Observed ~18% drop in steady-state residency on staging during synthetic replay. Will monitor for cache miss amplification. Canary rollout scheduled Thu.

ciaran: Ran GC churn experiments w/ alternate free-list strategy. Small object reuse improved but we see occasional 10-20% pause spikes when refill runs coincide with batch flush. Putting a leaky bucket limiter on batch flush to smooth peaks. Created a short runbook for measuring fragmentation and GC-induced pauses: https://docs.internal/frag-runbook.

kevin: Started a conservative canary (10% of traffic) with the new eviction policy + batcher sampler on 6 nodes. So far 2 nodes have been stable for 3h, 1 node showed a small memory blip and was auto-rolled back by the canary controller. Collecting logs and heap samples from the rolled-back node.

perf-bot: Auto summary: canary metrics (3h): median latency +1ms, p95 +4ms, mem-residency -12% on canary nodes, OOM alerts suppressed during sampling. Links: https://telemetry.internal/canary/1723456789.

elaine: Good progress. Quick asks:
- Sam: please turn the 6-hour continuous heap sampling into a scheduled job (nightly for a week) and surface the top 5 alloc sites in the canary dashboard.
- Munir: add an emergency eviction override (route-level) we can flip if we see cache miss amplification affecting latency.
- Ciaran: add a histogram for pause duration to the incident dashboard and tag any >5ms pauses.
- Kevin: keep the canary at 10% until we have two full 24h stable windows.

sam: Ack. I'll PR the sampler->dashboard pipeline and add a short README for how to download continuous heaps.

munir: Ack. Will add an override toggle (ops-only) and document expected behavior. ETA: Wed morning.

ciaran: On it. Adding pause histogram and an alert for >2 occurrences of >5ms in 1h.

kevin: Will hold canary. If we hit 2nd rollback, we'll scale to 0% and run deeper tracing.

elaine: Action item summary (quick):
1) sam: nightly continuous heap sampling + dashboard (owner: sam, due: Tue EOD)
2) munir: route-level eviction override toggle + docs (owner: munir, due: Wed AM)
3) ciaran: pause histogram + alerting (owner: ciaran, due: Wed EOD)
4) kevin: canary containment & rollback investigations (owner: kevin, ongoing)
5) team: reconvene Fri 11am for a short walk-through of collected artifacts.

sam: 👍 adding the heap dump retention note: keep 7 days by default to avoid storage blowup.

munir: Noted. Will add a telemetry tag so we can correlate eviction flips to latency regressions.

ciaran: Small note: if fragmentation doesn't improve after eviction tuning we should consider slab-size rebalancing as a follow-up.

elaine: Cool. I'll update the postmortem with these checkpoints and set the calendar invite for Fri 11am. If anyone can't make it, DM me. :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks — will post canary logs to the thread after the 24h window.

perf-bot: Reminder: scheduled nightly sampler will trigger first run Tue 00:30 UTC.

elaine: Closing this check-in for now. Leave any follow-ups in this thread so we keep the audit trail.
